findings.title: Severe Operating Profit De-escalation Masked by Prior-Year Impairment Reversal
findings.description: Group trading profit contracted by 31.4% from R4,218m in FY2024 to R2,892m in FY2025, and profit for the period declined 28.3% from R3,900m to R2,796m (basic EPS down 28.8% to 745.2 cents). While FY2024 was heavily distorted by a R1,019m non-operating intangible asset impairment reversal, underlying FY2025 gross profit grew by just 1.2% (R10,934m vs R10,805m) while trading expenses expanded 3.4% to R8,447m, revealing negative operational leverage.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Intangible asset impairment reversal: 2025: - | 2024: 1 019 Rm; Trading profit: 2025: 2 892 Rm | 2024: 4 218 Rm; Profit for the period: 2025: 2 796 Rm | 2024: 3 900 Rm; Basic earnings per share (cents): 2025: 745.2 | 2024: 1 046.9
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Operating margin, Normalized EBITDA, EPS growth rates
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Normalize FY2024 earnings base by removing the R1,019m non-cash trademark impairment reversal to assess true recurring operating profit growth and evaluate trading expense inflation relative to top-line growth.

findings.title: Substantial Credit Portfolio Exposure and Ongoing Credit Cost Drag
findings.description: Credit risk remains the sole Key Audit Matter. Truworths operates an unsecured credit book where the active trade receivables portfolio of R6,448m carries an ECL allowance of R1,339m (20.8% coverage), and the secondary 'charged-off' portfolio holds R543m with an ECL of R400m (73.7% coverage). In FY2025, trade receivable costs drained R1,260m (including R1,164m net bad debt and ECL provisions), absorbing 11.5% of total gross profit.
findings.source_section: Independent Auditor's Report - Key Audit Matter
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: As at 29 June 2025 the Group’s trade receivables active portfolio amounted to R6 448 million, against which an ECL allowance of R1 339 million has been raised. The “charged-off” trade receivables portfolio... amounted to R543 million, against which an ECL allowance of R400 million was raised.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Net bad debt expense, trade receivables impairment rate, gross credit margin
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Stress-test the forward-looking macroeconomic overlay and write-off timing assumptions used in the IFRS 9 ECL model, and track net bad debt write-offs relative to retail sales growth.

findings.title: Short-Term Debt Concentration and Negative Net Cash Position
findings.description: Non-current interest-bearing borrowings dropped to R0m (from R268m in FY2024), while current interest-bearing borrowings increased to R1,479m (from R1,208m). Together with the bank overdraft of R975m, Truworths faces R2,454m of debt obligations due within 12 months. Against cash and cash equivalents of R964m, net cash and cash equivalents stood in a deficit of -R11m at year-end, elevating short-term refinancing and rollover dependency.
findings.source_section: Group Statements of Financial Position / Note 12
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Non-current liabilities: Interest-bearing borrowings: - (2024: 268 Rm); Current liabilities: Interest-bearing borrowings: 1 479 Rm (2024: 1 208 Rm); Bank overdraft: 975 Rm (2024: 1 099 Rm); NET CASH AND CASH EQUIVALENTS AT THE REPORTING DATE: (11) Rm (2024: (298) Rm)
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Liquidity ratios, net interest expense, short-term debt refinancing risk
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Review Note 16 and Note 25 facility maturity schedules to confirm undrawn committed facilities, refinancing terms, and any applicable covenant headrooms on the R1.48bn short-term debt facility.

findings.title: Downplayed Macro Headwinds and Failure of Anticipated South African Consumer Recovery
findings.description: Management highlights disciplined margins and robust returns, but concedes that post-election sentiment and macroeconomic recovery in South Africa (accounting for 64% of group revenue) failed to materialize due to internal GNU friction and geopolitical tensions. Concurrently, UK consumer spending (accounting for 32% of group revenue) remains depressed by declining real disposable incomes since 2021 and high interest rates.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: However, much of this optimism failed to materialise due to a combination of geopolitical uncertainties - particularly around tariffs and rising tensions in the Middle East - and internal challenges within the GNU. Consequently, South Africa’s macroeconomic environment remained constrained... UK consumer spending remained subdued due to declining real disposable incomes since late 2021
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Same-store sales growth, discretionary consumer spending elasticity
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Re-evaluate medium-term revenue CAGR projections given the acknowledged lack of consumer rebound in South Africa and UK real wage stagnation.

findings.title: Inventory Shrinkage and Direct Write-offs Surged 102% Despite Lower Reported Provision Rate
findings.description: While management reports that markdown and shrinkage allowances fell from 15.3% to 13.6% of gross inventory (and 16.1% to 14.2% of finished goods), the actual inventory shrinkage and write-offs expensed directly into cost of sales doubled from R43 million in FY2024 to R87 million in FY2025. This indicates deteriorating stock loss/theft or rapid obsolescence that bypasses the balance sheet reserve.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: * During the reporting period inventory shrinkage and write offs to the value of R87 million (June 2024: R43 million) were expensed in cost of sales. Please refer to note 27.1.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Gross profit margin, cost of sales, shrinkage rate
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Adjust gross margin forecasts downward for elevated shrinkage and verify whether store-level shrinkage controls have structurally weakened.

findings.title: 100% of Interest-Bearing Borrowings Classified as Current Liabilities Alongside Heavy Uncommitted Overdraft
findings.description: Total interest-bearing borrowings of R1,479 million are now classified entirely as current liabilities (non-current borrowings fell to Rnil from R268 million). The R268 million green loan matures in December 2025, and the R1.2 billion revolving credit facility (fully drawn) operates on 12-month notice. Concurrently, the group utilizes a R975 million overdraft drawn against a facility where R1.7 billion of the R2.0 billion total is uncommitted, creating acute refinancing exposure.
findings.source_section: Note 16 - Interest-bearing borrowings & Note 12 - Cash and cash equivalents
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Non-current portion of interest-bearing borrowings - (2024: 268) / Current portion of interest-bearing borrowings 1,479 (2024: 1,208) ... The bank overdraft forms part of a South African Rand-based general short-term banking facility of R2 billion, of which R300 million is committed and R1.7 billion is uncommitted
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Short-term debt refinancing risk, liquidity ratios, finance costs
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Evaluate bank renewal commitments, covenant headroom, and potential step-up in lending margins upon refinancing in late 2025.

findings.title: Persistent High Debtors' Days (230 Days) and Rising Expected Credit Loss Ratios
findings.description: Debtors' collection period remains elevated at 230 days (FY2024: 229 days), reflecting high credit dependency. The ECL allowance against the active portfolio worsened from 20.3% to 20.8% (reaching R1,339 million), while the charged-off portfolio holds an additional R543 million gross receivables with a 73.7% allowance (R400 million).
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: The debtors’ days at the reporting date were 230 days (2024: 229 days)... Expected credit loss allowances to gross active trade receivables (%) 20.8 (2024: 20.3)
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Trade receivables turnover, bad debt expense, working capital cycle
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Scrutinize cash flow conversion and whether extended payment plans mask rising underlying default rates among retail credit customers.

findings.title: Office UK Impairment Reversal Headwinds and Cost-of-Living Strains
findings.description: Office UK carrying value of trademarks remains elevated at R1,398 million following a massive R1,019 million impairment reversal in FY2024. However, the notes acknowledge that the second half experienced notable expense inflation and decelerating sales growth due to the ongoing UK consumer cost-of-living crisis, creating potential vulnerability to future impairments.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: However, there was notable pressure on expense growth rates and a decline in sales growth rates during the second half of the 2024 reporting period, as the macro environment remains volatile and uncertain in light of the UK economic challenges and the continued decline in consumer spending on the back of the ongoing cost of living crisis.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Office UK revenue growth, store operating margins, intangible asset carrying value
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Stress-test the Office UK trademark recoverable amount against terminal growth rates lower than 1.4% and elevated UK retail wage/occupancy inflation.

findings.title: Restatement of Assets Incorrectly Classified at Fair Value Through OCI to P&L
findings.description: The group acknowledged an accounting classification error in prior reporting periods, restating financial assets previously reported as fair value through other comprehensive income (FVTOCI) to fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL). Additionally, presentation of lease liabilities was revised from other financial liabilities to amortised cost.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: In addition, we have restated assets which were incorrectly presented at fair value through other comprehensive income to assets held at fair value through profit or loss in the current financial period and have also applied this presentation change retrospectively.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Net finance income, other income volatility, equity reserves
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Assess whether prior-year earnings volatility was understated by bypassing P&L through OCI.

findings.title: Severe Margin Compression and Operating Profit Collapse in Truworths Africa and Group
findings.description: Segment reporting reveals a marked deterioration in operational profitability. Group trading profit collapsed 31.4% from R4,218 million to R2,892 million, with Truworths Africa trading profit contracting 16.0% (R1,529 million vs R1,820 million). Truworths Africa gross margin contracted by 130 bps from 54.9% to 53.6%, while group operating margin fell from 27.3% to 20.0%. Furthermore, South African third-party revenue declined from R14,898 million to R14,850 million, reflecting stagnant domestic top-line momentum.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Trading profit 1,529 [Truworths Africa] ... Trading profit 1,820 [2024] ... Gross margin (%) 53.6 [2024: 54.9] ... Operating margin (%) 20.4 [2024: 23.1] ... South Africa 14,850 [2024: 14,898]
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: EBITDA margin, trading profit margin, South African revenue growth forecasts
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Decompose domestic retail sales volume versus price increases, assess gross margin resistance against promotional discounting, and adjust medium-term African retail margin projections downwards.

findings.title: Surge in Current-Period Bad Debt Write-Offs and Total Debt Derecognition
findings.description: While headline net trade receivable costs appear flat (R1,260 million vs R1,310 million), the underlying credit quality shows severe stress. Amounts written off in respect of balances arising in the current period surged by 94.0% from R183 million in FY2024 to R355 million in FY2025. Across active and charged-off portfolios, balances written off totalled R1,024 million (R689 million active + R335 million charged-off). Total ECL allowance on trade receivables escalated to 24.9% (from 24.6%), and customers able to purchase slipped from 79% to 78%.

findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Credit loss expense ratio, debtor collection period, net bad debt provisions
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Incorporate higher credit impairment assumptions for FY2026 given that newly originated accounts are defaulting within the same annual cycle at twice the prior year's rate.

findings.title: Inventory Shrinkage and Write-Offs Doubled
findings.description: Buried inside the cost of sales note, inventory shrinkage and write-offs spiked by 102.3% from R43 million in FY2024 to R87 million in FY2025. This sharp rise points to potential internal controls, security, or distribution centre transition losses, eroding merchandise margins.

findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Gross margin, inventory loss provision, COGS bridge
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Inquire with management whether shrinkage increases stem from supply chain consolidation into the new distribution centre or elevated retail store theft.

findings.title: Overhead Cost Inflation: Administration and Occupancy Escalation
findings.description: Operating overheads outpaced top-line expansion significantly. Administration costs jumped 30.1% to R610 million (FY2024: R469 million), driving overall other operating costs up 11.2% to R1,771 million. In occupancy costs not accounted for under IFRS 16 (Note 27.4), expenses rose 6.8% to R1,145 million, exacerbated by a 67.3% surge in turnover-based lease expenses to R82 million (FY2024: R49 million) alongside persistent municipal and utility tariff inflation.
findings.source_section: Note 27.4 Occupancy costs & Note 27.6 Other operating costs

findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Operating expenditure inflation, administrative expenses-to-sales ratio
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Model structurally higher SG&A inflation given municipal tariff increases in South Africa and examine the specific drivers of the R141 million jump in administration expenses.

findings.title: Aggressive Depreciation Exemption on Distribution Centre and Imminent MHE Depreciation Drag
findings.description: For the new Truworths Africa Distribution Centre (TDC Airport), the Group incurred R171 million in capitalised construction costs via its 50% joint operation TREIC, but recognized zero depreciation on the building on the justification that 'the residual value of the building exceeds the cost thereof'. Additionally, R722 million was capitalised to plant and equipment for materials handling equipment (completed in FY2025). As MHE is commissioned, Truworths Africa will face incremental non-cash depreciation charges, compounding trading cost inflation.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: At the reporting date TREIC had incurred and capitalised construction and related costs in the amount of R171 million. No depreciation has been recognised as the residual value of the building exceeds the cost thereof ... R722 million had been incurred and capitalised to plant and equipment.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Depreciation and amortisation run-rate, PP&E carrying values, African segment operating margin
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Scrutinize the zero-depreciation policy for commercial real estate against accounting norms and add estimated annual depreciation for the R722 million materials handling equipment starting in FY2026.

findings.title: Dividend Cut of 7.9% Reflecting Earnings Contraction and Capital Commitments
findings.description: The Group cut its total annual dividend per share from 529 cents in FY2024 to 487 cents in FY2025 (with the final dividend cut by 13.7% from 197 cents to 170 cents). Total dividends declared fell from R2,204 million to R1,972 million, driven by the decline in headline earnings per share (752.1c vs 817.9c), elevated finance costs (up 10.3% to R525 million), and working capital/capex cash needs.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Dividends per share ... Final cash dividend - payable/paid September 170 197 ... Interim cash dividend - paid March 317 332 ... Total 487 529
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Dividend payout ratio, dividend yield, shareholder cash distributions
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Lower projected dividend yield expectations and reassess dividend cover targets in light of persistent earnings pressure and distribution centre financing obligations.

findings.title: Severe Downward Fair Value Revaluation of Core South African Subsidiary Truworths Ltd
findings.description: In the standalone company accounts, the fair value revaluation of direct subsidiaries recognised in other comprehensive income swung from a positive R10.54 billion gain in FY2024 to a massive R5.81 billion loss in FY2025. Specifically, the carrying valuation of the main trading subsidiary, Truworths Ltd (representing South African operations), was written down by R7.72 billion (from R26.80 billion to R19.08 billion), alongside write-downs in Young Designers Emporium (down R219m or 58%) and Truworths Trading (down R637m or 51%). This starkly reflects deteriorating peer EV/EBITDA multiples and operating performance expectations in the domestic retail core.

findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Standalone net asset value, subsidiary carrying values, SA retail segment EV/EBITDA multiples
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Examine the underlying EV/EBITDA multiples and DCF cash flow forecasts applied to the domestic business to confirm whether the South African retail segment faces long-term structural margin compression and derating relative to international operations.

findings.title: Parent Entity Guarantees for Subsidiary External Borrowings and Real Estate Debt
findings.description: The holding company acts as guarantor for external debt facilities entered into by Truworths Ltd as well as K2022434602 (South Africa) (Pty) Ltd (the real estate company holding 50% in the new Truworths Africa distribution centre). This exposes the parent balance sheet directly to external lender default risk and project debt covenants without debt being recognised on the standalone balance sheet.

findings.recommended_analyst_review: Cross-reference note 7 against Group debt disclosures to determine total external bank debt guaranteed and whether the new distribution centre project financing includes covenants or capital expenditure commitments.

findings.title: Declining Total Dividend Payout Per Share
findings.description: Declared dividends per share declined in FY2025 relative to prior periods: interim dividend dropped from 332 cents in 2024 to 317 cents in 2025, and the declared final dividend for 2025 dropped to 170 cents per share (compared to 197 cents for 2024 and 245 cents for 2023). Total dividends declared fell from R2.36 billion to R2.10 billion.

findings.recommended_analyst_review: Adjust forecast cash flow payout expectations down from historical run-rates to align with the 170 cps final dividend.

findings.title: Corporate Performance Target (CPT) Award Additions Contrast with Net Subsidiary Revaluation Losses
findings.description: Despite a R5.81 billion net fair value decline in subsidiaries and drop in dividend distribution, executive directors received 120,000 additional performance shares solely due to 'corporate performance targets (CPTs) being met', alongside 334,000 new PSP awards at strike R94.80. Key executives continue vesting and cashing out substantial PSP awards (e.g. Michael Mark vested and sold 301k awards for ~R32m and retained 345k awards).

findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Executive compensation alignment, share dilution
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Review remuneration report metrics to check whether long-term incentive CPT hurdles adequately reflect economic equity value degradation.

findings.title: Gross Margin Contraction and Negative Operating Leverage
findings.description: Cost of sales increased by 5% (R10,389m vs R9,859m), outpacing merchandise sales growth of only 3% (R21,323m vs R20,664m). This caused Group gross margin to contract by 100 bps from 52.3% to 51.3%. Concurrently, fixed overheads expanded well ahead of top-line growth, with occupancy costs climbing 7% (R1,145m vs R1,072m) and finance costs escalating 10% (R525m vs R476m), illustrating negative operating leverage across retail operations.
findings.source_section: Pro Forma Information - Statements of Comprehensive Income
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Gross profit margin, Operating margin, Retail operating expense growth assumptions
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Adjust forecast gross margins down by 100 bps and assess whether supply chain friction, promotional discounting, or input inflation will persist into FY2026, especially as occupancy costs continue to escalate at more than double sales growth.

findings.title: Normalized Earnings Contraction Masked by FY2024 One-Off Windfalls
findings.description: Reported FY2024 comparative earnings were heavily inflated by R1,284m of net non-recurring gains—chiefly a R1,019m partial reversal of Office UK trademark impairments, R122m net right-of-use asset impairment reversals, R123m operating cost reduction from first-time charitable trust consolidation, and R20m burglary insurance recoveries. Once stripped of these unrepeatable items, pro forma trading profit still fell 1% (R2,909m vs R2,934m) and pro forma HEPS declined 4% (from 780.8 cents to 752.1 cents). Structured data extractions misinterpret the R1,284m adjustment and the -31% reported trading profit delta.
findings.source_section: Pro Forma Information - Basis of preparation
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: The Group’s prior period earnings were enhanced by the following once-off events/transactions, making the prior period reported figures less comparable to the current period (and hence the pro forma adjustments): • a trademark impairment reversal in relation to the Office UK trademark (R1 019 million); • a net right of use asset impairment reversal (R122 million)... • insurance recoveries in Office UK (R20 million)... • a reduction in other operating costs (R123 million) resulting from the consolidation of the Group's charitable trusts for the first time.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Normalized EBITDA, Sustainable HEPS base, Non-operating income
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Ensure base-year FY2024 modeling strips out the R1,284m pre-tax windfalls to avoid understating the multi-year stagnation in underlying retail core operational profitability.

findings.title: Reversal of Store Portfolio Health: Net ROU Asset Impairments Resume
findings.description: After recording a net ROU asset impairment reversal of R121m/R122m in FY2024, store lease performance reversed back to net impairment in FY2025 with R17m in net impairments (R35m new impairments booked in operating costs offset by R18m reversals in other income). This swing highlights renewed store-level performance pressures in marginal retail locations.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: The amounts in the 2025 'Pro forma adjustments' column relate to the net right-of-use asset impairments (R35 million impairment accounted for in other operating costs and R18 million impairment reversal accounted for in other income)
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Store impairment charges, Right-of-use asset carrying values, Store fleet ROIC
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Evaluate store fleet rationalization plans and assess whether lease renewal terms or regional store traffic declines will trigger larger write-downs in future cycles.

findings.title: Substantial Institutional Divestment by Anchor Global Asset Managers
findings.description: Shareholder register disclosures reveal aggressive portfolio liquidations by prominent institutional asset managers between FY2024 and FY2025. Ninety One completely dropped below the 3% disclosure threshold (having held 8.9% / 36.2m shares in FY2024), BlackRock dropped below 3% (from 3.0% / 12.3m shares), and Old Mutual Investment Group halved its position from 8.3% (33.9m shares) to 4.6% (18.8m shares). This sharp institutional selling pressure was absorbed primarily by state pension funds (PIC/GEPF) and bank nominee blocks.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Old Mutual Investment Group South Africa 18,825,755 4.6 33,932,208 8.3 ... Ninety One* South Africa - - 36,208,719 8.9 ... BlackRock* United States of America - - 12,280,212 3.0
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Share overhang, Cost of equity, Institutional market sentiment
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Monitor potential overhang risk as major active institutional funds cut exposure, evaluating if selling was driven by ESG considerations, B-BBEE criteria, or structural concerns over SA apparel credit retail.

The interest in the insurance cell is represented by an investment in 1 C1 Class variable rate redeemable profit participating

capital adequacy requirements (CAR) as determined by various regulatory bodies and Old Mutual Insure. If the Group fails to

financially sound position. The Group does not carry insurance risk with regard to the insurance cell captive as any claims in
